material_systems.name: Oil-Based Penetrating Stain
example_products: General Finishes Oil Based Gel Stain
material_systems.notes: Traditional oil-based stain. Deep penetration, rich color. Longer dry time (4-8 hrs). Strong odor — ventilation required. Mineral spirits cleanup.

material_systems.name: Oil-Modified Stain (VOC-Compliant)
example_products: Sherwin-Williams Wood Classics Interior Oil Stain
material_systems.notes: VOC-compliant oil-modified formula. Similar penetration to traditional oil. Lower odor. Water cleanup.

material_systems.name: Water-Based Stain
example_products: General Finishes Water Based Wood Stain
material_systems.notes: Fast dry (1-2 hrs). Low odor. Water cleanup. Grain raise likely — conditional grain-raise prep task activated. Non-yellowing.

material_systems.name: Gel Stain
material_systems.notes: Gel formula sits on surface — does not penetrate deeply. Controls blotch on softwood without conditioner. QT4+ only (premium product). Thicker application, more even color. Does not require wood conditioner on softwood.

material_systems.name: Oil-Based Sanding Sealer
material_systems.notes: Shellac-based sanding sealer. Excellent adhesion promoter between stain and clear. Sands easily to smooth surface. Fast dry (30-60 min). Compatible with all clear coat types.

material_systems.name: Water-Based Sanding Sealer
example_products: General Finishes Water Based Sanding Sealer
Target Coatings Water Based Sanding Sealer
material_systems.notes: Water-based sanding sealer. Low odor. Fast dry. Sands smoothly. Best paired with WB clear coat but compatible with all types.

material_systems.name: Oil-Based Polyurethane
material_systems.notes: Traditional oil poly. Warm amber tone. Excellent durability. Longer dry time (4-6 hrs between coats). Mineral spirits cleanup. Yellows slightly over time.

material_systems.name: Water-Based Polyurethane
example_products: General Finishes High Performance Water Based Topcoat
material_systems.notes: Water-based poly. Crystal clear (no yellowing). Fast dry (2 hrs between coats). Low odor. Water cleanup. Good durability. May raise grain on first coat if no sealer used.

material_systems.name: Lacquer
example_products: Target Coatings EM6000 Water White Lacquer
material_systems.notes: Spray-only application. Fastest dry time (30-60 min between coats). Crystal clear. Excellent sandability. Professional-grade finish. Requires proper ventilation and respiratory protection. Pre-catalyzed lacquer preferred for durability.

coverage_profiles.notes: Stain brush application on bare wood trim. Varies by wood porosity — softwood absorbs more (lower coverage). 1 LF trim = 1 SF per PCA standard.
Stain roll application. Higher coverage rate than brush due to faster application. Some waste from wipe-off excess.
Stain spray application. Highest coverage rate but includes overspray waste. Still requires wipe step.
Sanding sealer — thin coat application. High spread rate. Applied over stained or bare wood.
Clear coat brush application. Similar to paint coverage on smooth substrate. Applied over sealer or previous clear coat.
Clear coat spray application. Higher transfer efficiency than paint spray due to thinner mil thickness.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 120-grit
consumables.usage: Initial bare wood sanding — removes mill marks, opens grain
consumables.notes: First pass on bare wood. 120 grit for initial stock removal and mill mark elimination.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-grit
consumables.usage: Final bare wood prep sanding — smooth surface for stain acceptance
consumables.notes: Second pass on bare wood. 150 grit creates smooth surface for uniform stain absorption.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.notes: Between sealer coats. Levels sealer for smooth clear coat application.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.usage: Final sealer sand, clear coat interstage sanding (QT4)
consumables.notes: Between clear coats at QT4. Final sealer sand before clear. Fine grit for smooth finish.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 400-grit
consumables.notes: Between clear coats at QT5. Ultra-fine for glass-smooth finish between coats.

consumables.name: Foam brush (2")
consumables.usage: Stain application — affordable disposable applicator for stain
consumables.notes: Disposable foam brushes for stain application. One per stain session. Good for even stain distribution.

consumables.name: Stain wipe cloth (lint-free rags)
consumables.usage: Wipe excess stain after application — controls color depth and uniformity
consumables.notes: Lint-free cotton rags for wiping excess stain. Critical consumable — stain wipe controls final color. Multiple rags per session.

consumables.name: Foam roller (4" mini)
consumables.usage: Stain roll application — lint-free foam avoids fibers in stain
consumables.notes: Foam mini rollers for stain application. Lint-free — avoids fiber contamination in stain coat.

consumables.name: Natural bristle brush (2-2.5")
consumables.notes: Natural bristle (China bristle) for oil-based polyurethane. Do NOT use with water-based products (bristles swell).

consumables.name: Synthetic bristle brush (2-2.5")
consumables.usage: Water-based clear coat and sealer brush application
consumables.notes: Nylon/polyester blend for water-based clear coat and sealer. Also suitable for water-based stains.

consumables.name: Pre-stain wood conditioner
consumables.usage: Softwood conditioning before stain — prevents blotchy absorption
consumables.notes: Applied to softwood (pine, poplar, alder) before stain to even absorption. Not needed for hardwood or gel stain. Apply, wait 15 min, wipe excess.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.usage: Remove sanding dust before each coat application
consumables.notes: One tack cloth covers ~200 LF of trim. Use before every coat for dust-free surface. Critical for clear coat quality.

consumables.name: Straining cone (paper)
consumables.usage: Strain clear coat before application to remove debris
consumables.notes: Paper straining cones to filter clear coat. Prevents dust and dried particles from contaminating clear finish. One per pour.

consumables.name: Mineral spirits
consumables.usage: Cleanup for oil-based stain and oil-based polyurethane
consumables.notes: For oil-based product cleanup. Not needed when using all water-based products.

consumables.name: Masking tape (1.5" blue painter's tape)
consumables.usage: Wall masking at trim edge (spray method, or any method when walls are SS_PAINTED_*)
consumables.notes: 60 yards = 180 LF per roll. Used for wall_adjacent zone masking and fixture covers.

consumables.name: Masking paper (12")
consumables.usage: Wall masking adjacent to trim during spray
consumables.notes: 60 yards = 180 LF per roll. 12" width covers wall adjacent to trim.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth runner
consumables.notes: Runner-style drops along trim work area. 1-2 per painter, reusable. Stain drips are especially hard to clean — protection critical.

consumables.name: Stainable wood filler
consumables.usage: Fill nail holes, dents, and defects in bare wood before staining
consumables.notes: STAINABLE wood filler — NOT spackle. Regular spackle does not accept stain evenly. Use color-matched filler for best results.

floor_perimeter.description: Drop cloth runners along trim work area perimeter
floor_perimeter.notes: Stain drips are harder to clean than paint — floor protection is especially important.

wall_adjacent.notes: Required for spray to protect wall. Also required when walls are SS_PAINTED_* with any method.

fixture_covers.notes: Tape over nearby outlets and switches when spraying.

compatibility_rules.description: No chemistry-pairing constraints between stain and clear layers
compatibility_rules.notes: Oil stain under WB clear is standard practice. Any stain works under any sealer works under any clear. Only hard constraints are gel stain QT gate and lacquer spray-only.
Gel stain is a premium product. Blocked below QT4.
Lacquer dries too fast for brush application. Spray only.

material_notes.selection_guidance: Material systems are organized by product_role (stain, sealer, clear). No chemistry-pairing constraints — any stain under any sealer under any clear is valid. Only 2 hard rules: gel stain requires QT4+, lacquer requires spray. Contractor retains discretion on product selection.
material_notes.stain_wipe_critical: ALL stain application methods include a wipe step. Stain sits on surface and penetrates — excess must be wiped to control color depth and prevent blotchy appearance. Wipe timing varies by stain type (oil: 5-15 min, WB: 1-3 min, gel: 3-5 min).
material_notes.coverage_note: Coverage uses PDCA standard: 1 LF trim = 1 SF coverage area for standard profile. Wood porosity significantly affects stain coverage — softwood absorbs more than hardwood.
material_notes.grain_raise: Water-based products (WB stain, WB sealer, WB clear) may raise wood grain on bare wood. Grain-raise prep task conditionally activated to prevent rough texture in final finish.
